**Finding: missing** (INSURANCE — Vendor insurance)

**Investigation.** Document-wide searches for `insurance`, `insur` and `indemnif` returned zero hits. I read the full General Provisions block (Section 10, p0059–p0070) and the operative responsibilities/confidentiality sections to rule out an embedded covenant — the miscellaneous section covers notices, no joint venture, assignment, waiver, governing law, severability, survival, entire agreement and headings, but nothing on insurance.

**Why the rule bites.** HDI is squarely a services/hosting vendor within scope:
- It designs, hosts and maintains the Site on its own server (p0005, p0007).
- Section 8.1 (p0048) expressly contemplates HDI having access to "Content, user information, data" and Confidential Information of the Company.

A vendor that hosts our site and processes user data with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under the rule, not a mere sub-element gap — so an insertion is warranted rather than a rationale-only note.

**Redline.** Inserted new Section 10.9 (Insurance) after p0070, at the end of General Provisions and before the execution block, at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M (scoped to the period HDI hosts the Site or holds Confidential Information or user data), statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request. The one-year tail sits comfortably inside existing Section 10.7 survival (p0068), which already carries Section 10 for two years post-termination. The comment offers the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) as a landing zone. Redline validated `ok:true`; finding submitted at 0.9 confidence.
